name: Mukhyamantri Kanya Sumangala Yojana
applies_to: Women and girls resident in Uttar Pradesh (UP domicile), subject to the eligibility below.
department: Directorate of Women Welfare, Department of Women & Child Development, Govt of UP
verification: Verified on an official government source
benefit:
Up to ₹25,000 per girl, paid by DBT in 6 stages: ₹5,000 at birth (born on or after 1 Apr 2019); ₹2,000 after full
immunisation within 1 year; ₹3,000 on admission to Class 1; ₹3,000 on admission to Class 6; ₹5,000 on
admission to Class 9; ₹7,000 on admission to a degree or a diploma of 2 years or more after passing Class
10/12. (Older myScheme page still shows the pre-2024 total of ₹15,000; the official MKSY portal shows
₹25,000.)
eligibility:
• The family must live in Uttar Pradesh and have residence proof (ration card, Aadhaar, voter ID, electricity
bill or telephone bill is accepted).
• Annual family income must be ₹3 lakh or less.
• The family must have at most 2 children.
• At most 2 girls from one family can get the benefit.
• If the second delivery gives twins, a girl born as the third child is also eligible.
• If the first delivery is a girl and the second delivery gives twin girls, all three girls are eligible.
• An adopted orphan girl is counted with the biological children; at most 2 girls per family in total.
• Aadhaar of the applicant, father, mother and the girl is mandatory since 10 Oct 2022.
documents:
• Latest photo of the girl (all stages).
• Joint photo of the girl with the applicant (all stages).
• Self-declaration/affidavit in the prescribed format (all stages).
• Stage 1 (birth): birth certificate of the girl.
• Stage 2 (immunisation): immunisation card.
• Stage 3: Class 1 admission certificate.
• Stage 4: Class 6 admission certificate.
• Stage 5: Class 9 admission certificate.
• Stage 6: Class 10/12 marksheet or certificate, institution ID, and degree/diploma admission fee receipt.
• Aadhaar of the applicant, father, mother and the girl (mandatory since 10 Oct 2022).
Source of documents list: myscheme
how_to_apply:
Online: go to mksy.up.gov.in > Citizen Services Portal (Apply Here), register with Aadhaar and mobile OTP, log
in with the user ID sent by SMS, fill the girl's form, upload documents and submit. Applications are verified by
the Block Development Officer / SDM and approved by the District Probation Officer.
window: Open all year; apply within the current academic session for school/college stages.
current_status:
ACTIVE. Official portal live and accepting applications (checked 23 Oct 2026); scheme running since 1 Apr
2019.

name: UP Pre-Matric Scholarship (Class 9–10)
applies_to: Women and girls resident in Uttar Pradesh (UP domicile), subject to the eligibility below.
department: Social Welfare Dept (SC/ST/General), Backward Classes Welfare Dept (OBC), Minority Welfare Dept, Govt of UP
verification: Verified on an official government source
benefit:
Yearly scholarship paid to the student's Aadhaar-linked bank account. Rates per official/myScheme pages:
General ₹3,000 a year; SC/ST ₹3,500 a year (day scholar) or ₹7,000 (hosteller); OBC ₹150 a month for 10
months plus ₹750 ad-hoc grant (up to ₹2,250 a year). Girls and boys are both eligible.
eligibility:
• Student must be a resident of Uttar Pradesh studying in Class 9 or 10 in a recognised school in UP.
• Age 12 to 20 years on 1 July (per myScheme).
• Income limit for SC and ST students: family income up to ₹2.5 lakh a year.
• Income limit for General category: ₹2 lakh a year (the myScheme page for General Pre-Matric shows ₹2.5
lakh – confirm on the portal for your class).
• Income limit for OBC students: ₹2 lakh a year (as on the Backward Classes Welfare Dept page; a Feb 2026
report said the Class 9–10 OBC limit is being raised to ₹2.5 lakh – not confirmed by an official order).
• Income limit for Minority students: ₹2 lakh a year.
• A proposal (Amar Ujala, 4 Apr 2026) to double limits to ₹4 lakh (General/OBC/Minority) and ₹5 lakh
(SC/ST) is NOT yet approved.
• Student cannot take another scholarship at the same time (some exceptions).
documents:
• Aadhaar card (bank account must be Aadhaar-seeded/NPCI-mapped).
• Income certificate of the family from e-District (Tehsil).
• Caste certificate from e-District (for SC, ST and OBC students).
• UP residence proof.
• Marksheet of the last exam passed.
• Fee receipt / admission proof of the current year (if fee is charged).
• Enrolment/registration number from the school or college.
• Bank passbook copy of the student's own account.
• Recent passport-size photo.
• OTR (One Time Registration) number – mandatory from 2025-26.
Source of documents list: myscheme
how_to_apply:
Do OTR on scholarship.up.gov.in, then register and fill the Pre-Matric (Fresh or Renewal) form, upload
documents, complete Aadhaar/NPCI checks, take the final printout and submit it with attachments at your
school. The school and District Inspector of Schools verify it.

applies_to: Women and girls resident in Uttar Pradesh (UP domicile), subject to the eligibility below.
department: Women Welfare Department, Govt of UP (applications on the Integrated Pension Portal SSPY-UP)
aka: Pati ki Mrityu-uprant Nirashrit Mahila Pension Yojana, UP Vidhwa Pension
verification: Verified on an official government source
benefit:
₹1,000 per month per woman, paid by DBT/PFMS into the bank account (in quarterly instalments). The
amount was raised from ₹500 to ₹1,000 by GO dated 17 Dec 2021. A rise to ₹1,500 has been reported as under
consideration in 2026, but no Cabinet approval or GO was found as of 23 Oct 2026.
eligibility:
• The applicant must be a permanent resident of Uttar Pradesh.
• The applicant's husband must have died.
• The applicant must be at least 18 years old.
• The annual income of the applicant and her family from all sources must not exceed ₹2 lakh.
• The applicant must not be receiving a pension from any other state or central government scheme.
Not eligible:
• Women already getting a pension under another state or central scheme.
• Pension stops if the woman remarries; pension paid after the remarriage date is recovered.
• Families with annual income above ₹2 lakh.
• Note: the ₹46,080 (rural) / ₹56,460 (urban) income limits often quoted for this pension actually belong to
the UP old-age pension, not to this scheme.
documents:

• Mobile number linked with Aadhaar.
• Self-declaration (shapath-patra) that she is not receiving a pension under any similar state or central

Officer (BDO) and urban applications by the SDM/City Magistrate. The District Probation Officer and a district

for 4 years), plus a 10% margin-money subsidy on project cost (max ₹50,000; paid back-ended). Phase 2 (after

all applicants in aspirational or backward districts) of the project cost.
Not eligible:
• Anyone who has already received an interest or capital subsidy under any central or state scheme (PM
SVANidhi is exempted).
• Anyone currently taking benefits under another central or state loan-subsidy scheme.

aka: JSY, Safe motherhood scheme under National Health Mission

benefit:
One-time cash for delivery in a government or accredited private hospital (mother's package). Low Performing
States (LPS): ₹1,400 in rural areas and ₹1,000 in urban areas. High Performing States (HPS): ₹700 in rural
areas and ₹600 in urban areas. North-Eastern States (except Assam) and rural areas of tribal districts of other
states: ₹700. BPL women who deliver at home get ₹500 per delivery. Free delivery, medicines, tests, diet and
transport are given separately under Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK). LPS are UP, Uttarakhand,
Bihar, Jharkhand, MP, Chhattisgarh, Assam, Rajasthan, Odisha and J&K; all other states/UTs are HPS.
eligibility:
• Pregnant woman who delivers in a government health facility (Sub-centre approved for delivery, PHC, CHC,
FRU, or general ward of a District/State hospital) or in an accredited private health institution.
• In Low Performing States: all pregnant women delivering in a government health facility are eligible; no
marriage or BPL certificate is needed.
• In High Performing States: the woman must be from a BPL household or be an SC/ST woman.
• For delivery in an accredited private hospital (any state): the woman must be BPL or SC/ST and carry a
referral slip from the ASHA/ANM/Medical Officer.
• For home delivery (any state): only BPL pregnant women, with a BPL certificate; ₹500 is paid.

Not eligible:

• Payments made earlier or later than 7 days around delivery are treated as irregular.
